title: Converge Docker bases and introduce build-cache profiles to reduce CI noise
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Problem: Over the last 18 months we've accumulated a set of slightly different Docker base images (node-builder, node-runtime, python-builder, slim-runtime, proprietary-ubuntu variants). The duplication causes frequent cache misses in CI, large pushed artifacts, and a combinatorial explosion of layer diffs when we tweak common dependencies (causing long rebuilds across many repos). Several repos still use deprecated linter/toolchain versions which invalidates caches and produces inconsistent lint failures.

Proposal: Consolidate to a small set of standardized base images (builder-base and runtime-base) that are multi-arch and kept minimal. Introduce explicit 'build-cache profiles' for CI (hot, warm, cold) and enable registry-backed BuildKit cache export/import for GitHub Actions and internal runners. Standardize and pin toolchain versions (Node 20.x, Go 1.20+, python 3.11) via dockerfile-toolchain-manifest, and upgrade linters (eslint, golangci-lint) to supported stable releases. Update CI workflows to use transient cache keys and a stable cache priming job.

Goals / Acceptance criteria:
- Reduce median CI full-build time by >= 35% for impacted repos on first successful incremental run.
- Increase registry cache hit rate from ~40% to >= 75% within one month of rollout.
- Decrease average Docker layer size across runtime images by >= 20%.
- All monorepos using new images and toolchain manifests (tracked via repo check and CI badge).

Out-of-scope: Rewriting all Dockerfiles to use distroless or switching to a different build system entirely. That work will be a follow-up once we have stable base images.
plan: Audit existing Dockerfiles across top-50 active repos and categorize: builder vs runtime vs special-case
Design two minimal base images (builder-base, runtime-base) with reproducible builds and reproducible timestamps
Create dockerfile-toolchain-manifest in infra repo that pins node/go/python and linter versions
Enable BuildKit remote cache for GH Actions and internal runners; add a dedicated cache-priming job
Update sample repo (platform/infra) to use new bases + cache profiles and prove CI improvements
Rollout to remaining repos in waves; track metrics and provide opt-out guidance for special cases
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Some repos need custom native deps that won't fit the minimal base. Mitigation: provide a documented extension layer pattern and a 'special-case' base with clear cost reasons.
Risk: Cache secrecy and credentials when using registry-backed cache. Mitigation: use short-lived tokens, restrict cache pushes to CI service account, audit pushes.
Risk: Linter/Tooling upgrades may introduce large number of fixes. Mitigation: run linters in quiet/fix modes, schedule bulk-fix cadence with PMs, and provide autofix PRs where safe.
migration_steps: Week 1: Repo audit + inventory + design doc (link below)
Week 2: Build initial builder-base/runtime-base images and publish to staging registry
Week 3: Implement BuildKit cache export/import in CI templates and add cache-priming workflow
Week 4-6: Migrate 10 repos per week (start with infra/tooling, then platform services, then user-facing SDKs)
Post-migration: Monitor cache-hit metrics, iterate on base images, and lock manifests for stability
metrics_to_track: CI median build wall time (pre/post) - primary metric
Number of lint failures introduced by tool upgrades
